tasks.goal: Provide one release-local selection-only fuzzy suggestion component and option contract.
input_facts: The four list views currently use plain el-input keyword controls.
Element Plus el-select is already installed and used throughout the release module.
No existing shared component separates temporary filter text from a stable selected option.
invariants: No allow-create or arbitrary free-text model value is introduced.
Temporary text does not emit update:modelValue.
Styles remain scoped to the release module and semantic theme variables.
interface_contracts: ReleaseSearchOption has value, label, description and keywords.
ReleaseSearchSelect emits update:modelValue only for real selection or clear and emits search for temporary queries.
non_goals: No backend API or dependency change.
action_bounds: Add only the release-local component, option type and related CSS.
Use existing Vue 3 and Element Plus capabilities.
acceptance_checks: Static inspection confirms no allow-create and a 20-option limit.
Temporary query and stable model state are separate.
evidence_required: actual diff for the three scoped files
tasks.rollback: Delete ReleaseSearchSelect.vue and restore the task-added type and CSS block.
stop_conditions: The installed Element Plus version cannot separate filter text from selected values.
Implementation requires modifying public components outside the release module.
escalation_conditions: A dependency upgrade or platform-wide component contract becomes necessary.

tasks.goal: Integrate real-record fuzzy selection into release windows, production baseline and current production lists.
input_facts: ReleaseWindowView receives a complete current-project windows array and can select by window id.
ReleaseBaselineView receives a complete selected-window entry array and can select by entry id.
ReleaseCurrentProductionView receives a complete current-project production entry array and can select by entry id.
invariants: Existing status, production-result and artifact-type filters remain composable.
Selection uses exact record ids after fuzzy candidate filtering.
Scope refresh clears a selected id that no longer exists.
No extra backend candidate request is added.
interface_contracts: Each view maps its real loaded records to ReleaseSearchOption.
Each rows computation filters by stable selected id and existing independent filters.
non_goals: No change to window CRUD or baseline maintenance.
action_bounds: Replace only the three list keyword states/templates/filters.
Add watchers only to invalidate stale selections after scope changes.
acceptance_checks: vue-tsc passes after all three integrations.
Typing without selection leaves rows unchanged.
Selecting an option filters to its exact record and clearing restores rows under other filters.
Only the application legacy search input remains after T2.
evidence_required: actual diff for the three scoped views
targeted rg result for remaining legacy input
tasks.rollback: Restore each view's previous keyword ref, includes-based rows filter, Search icon import and el-input template.
stop_conditions: A local data source is discovered to be truncated for its current scope.
A selected value cannot be invalidated without changing business data flow.
escalation_conditions: A new backend suggestion endpoint becomes necessary for any local view.

tasks.goal: Provide debounced project-scoped application suggestions without mutating the main list until selection and complete cross-page verification.
input_facts: ReleaseApplicationView currently debounces keyword changes directly into the main-list query.
ReleaseManagementPrototype owns application pagination, status and list API loading.
listReleaseApplications already supports page, size, projectId and keyword.
Browser evidence proves the existing backend keyword predicate omits subsystem_code while exact application-code matching works.
invariants: Candidate loading, error and records remain separate from main-list state.
Candidate query is page 1, size 20 and current-project scoped.
The existing parameterized keyword predicate covers application code, subsystem code and subsystem name.
Only selected applicationCode is sent to the main list keyword.
Status filtering and pagination keep existing behavior.
Older candidate responses cannot overwrite newer results.
interface_contracts: ReleaseApplicationView consumes candidate options/loading/error and emits search-options for temporary text.
ReleaseManagementPrototype provides a 300ms debounced generation-guarded candidate query using listReleaseApplications.
non_goals: No API endpoint or backend query semantics change.
No application CRUD, workflow or approval change.
No changes outside the release module.
action_bounds: Replace the application keyword watcher with selected application-code handling.
Add isolated candidate request state, debounce cleanup and project-switch invalidation in the parent.
Correct only the missing subsystem_code OR predicate and add a focused contract assertion.
Run build, diff checks and authenticated browser verification.
acceptance_checks: The focused release application persistence contract test passes.
No legacy release list search el-input remains.
All four pages show first 20 on empty focus, fuzzy-filter candidates, ignore unselected text, apply selection and restore on clear.
Rapid application input does not mutate the main list or allow stale candidates to win.
evidence_required: actual diff for application view and parent
production build output and exit code
browser row, option, request and console observations
tasks.rollback: Restore ReleaseApplicationView's keyword watcher, remove parent candidate state/provider, and remove the subsystem_code predicate/test assertion; then reverse T2 and T1 in dependency order if full rollback is required.
stop_conditions: The existing API cannot return project-scoped fuzzy candidates.
Runtime authentication or backend availability prevents browser observation after build succeeds.
Implementation requires changes outside the approved release frontend scope.
escalation_conditions: A backend API contract or dependency change becomes necessary.
